sections.title: The Letter Elle
paragraphs: The letter (elle) /ˈɛlle/ makes the sound /l/, like in the word (luna) /ˈlu.na/, which means moon. This letter always represents one single sound in Italian words.

sections.title: Pronouncing Elle
paragraphs: Press the tip of your tongue against your upper gum ridge, right behind your front teeth. Let the air flow smoothly past both sides of your tongue while you voice the sound. Touch your throat to feel your vocal cords vibrate.

sections.title: Reading Rules
paragraphs: This letter always makes the sound /l/ in all positions. You can hear it clearly in the word (sole) /ˈso.le/.

sections.title: Common Pitfalls
paragraphs: Do not pull the back of your tongue down as in the English word ball. Keep your tongue tip light and flat behind your teeth, like in the English word leaf.
